## 2. DNS records to add

Values copied from Defender → Email authentication settings → DKIM → *click the domain name* → Create DKIM keys. Note the shard letters differ per domain — the first domain's pattern was **not** reused for the second.

| Domain | Host | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| example.com | `_dmarc` | TXT | `v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@example.com` |
| example.com | `selector1._domainkey` | CNAME | `selector1-example-com._domainkey.<tenant>.n-v1.dkim.mail.microsoft` |
| example.com | `selector2._domainkey` | CNAME | `selector2-example-com._domainkey.<tenant>.n-v1.dkim.mail.microsoft` |
| example.com.au | `_dmarc` | TXT | `v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@example.com` |
| example.com.au | `selector1._domainkey` | CNAME | `selector1-example-com-au._domainkey.<tenant>.r-v1.dkim.mail.microsoft` |
| example.com.au | `selector2._domainkey` | CNAME | `selector2-example-com-au._domainkey.<tenant>.r-v1.dkim.mail.microsoft` |

The blog-post `.onmicrosoft.com` CNAMEs on `example.com` were removed — they resolved to nothing useful, which is why the toggle failed.

## 4. Enable + tighten plan

1. **Enable `example.com.au` first** — Microsoft has never looked it up, so no negative cache; enabled on the first click.
2. **`example.com`:** the toggle failed "CNAME record does not exist" 25 minutes after the correct records were live (Microsoft's resolvers negative-cached the earlier miss from the wrong CNAMEs). No DNS change; retried after ~70 minutes → enabled.
3. Send test mail from each domain; confirm `dkim=pass` and `dmarc=pass` in received headers.
4. After two weeks of clean aggregate reports: `p=quarantine`, then `p=reject`.
